newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse to consider BRE warrants.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse to consider BRE warrants.

text.p: The next meeting of the Warsaw bourse's board in late August might consider Polish Bank Rozwoju Eksportu's (BRE) proposal that its warrants be listed, the bourse's president said on Friday.
"At the next board meeting in late August we plan either to discuss warrant trade once again or submit a specific proposal," Wieslaw Rozlucki told reporters.

BRE has so far issued call warrants for non-public trade on Polish stocks -- mostly high-turnover blue chips and trading in the continuous system -- mass privatisation NFI units, treasury bonds and T- bills.
Earlier this month the bourse said warrants might start trade at the end of this year's third quarter.
In May the bourse approved rules paving the way for trade in warrants on shares and bonds in the large-cap WIG 20 index, stock indices and exchange and interest rates.
The bourse said the minimum size of the warrant issue would be 10,000 and their expiry period should not be shorter than three months.
The minium value of the underlying bonds or shares was set at three million zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
